Who to hold accountable — unpaid wages, wrongful dismissal, financial losses — filing complaints, arbitration, or lawsuits instead of taking revenge

Read the document thoroughly before signing; never sign on behalf of others or on blank paper
Write a clear loan agreement when lending money; think carefully before agreeing to be a guarantor
Time limits for legal action: 3 years for civil lawsuits, 1 year for labor arbitration; once the deadline passes, a simple “statute of limitations exceeded” claim can block your case

If you’re subject to spending restrictions or listed on the dishonesty registry, first find out which rule applies and request removal if possible
If scammed while shopping online or via second-hand markets, first file a complaint with the platform, then report it to police, and finally decide whether to sue
Think carefully before and after making large gifts in romantic relationships or marriage
Transfer betrothal gifts via payment with clear notes; keep chat records; money demanded under marriage can be reclaimed
No need to worry about premarital assets — clearly define property additions and parental contributions
Check a person’s marital status before getting married; those who use marriage as a pretext to defraud money can be prosecuted for fraud
For home appliance repairs, vehicle inspections, and renovations: always ask for a quote first and stay on site throughout the process
Don’t be a “nominal legal representative” — don’t lend your ID to register a company

If the other person is intoxicated, unconscious, or under 14, do not have sex with them
If someone threatens to call the police, post intimate photos, or inform your workplace unless you pay up — don’t give them a single cent and don’t delete any records; call the police right away
If someone falsely accuses you, you can seek legal consequences: up to 5 days of detention for minor violations, up to 3 years in prison for criminal acts
Insufficient evidence alone warrants acquittal; coerced confessions must be excluded; appeals and retrials remain possible after conviction

For individuals released from detention after a case is dropped, charges are withdrawn, or they are acquitted, applying for state compensation is possible — compensation is calculated on a daily basis

The legal route of “buying insurance for a family member first, then harming them” is completely blocked: you get zero money, and the perpetrator faces multiple charges including intentional homicide and insurance fraud

You must obtain a case receipt when reporting a crime; if no case is opened, you must receive a written notice. You can request a reconsideration within 7 days and a review within another 7 days. The procuratorate can also order the police to open a case
Don’t give money or cards to investigators, law enforcers: offering bribes is a crime, and bribing oversight, law enforcement, and judicial staff is punished even more severely

Family members have gambling debts; don't rush to pay them for them: Gambling debts are not protected by law, and money borrowed for gambling does not count as common marital debt

Leashing dogs is mandatory: failure to do so means strict liability for any harm caused (you must pay compensation regardless of fault), and the obligation extends fully. The dog also needs its rabies vaccinations on schedule and a dog registration

If a dog injures someone, the owner generally has to pay no matter who was at fault; only proof that the other person acted intentionally or with gross negligence can reduce it. Without a leash, “the other person's intent” is the only reduction left, and in serious cases you can also be detained. A dog without its rabies shots on schedule brings an order to correct it and possibly a fine. For prohibited aggressive breeds there is no ground for exemption at all.

Cost

A leash costs a few dozen yuan. Rabies vaccination and registration also cost money, with fees varying by locality in China. The difficulty is remembering the leash every time you go out and taking the dog for vaccination when due.
Benefit

In China, when a kept animal injures someone, its owner or keeper at the time must compensate them; the legal term is tort liability. Only proof that the injured person deliberately provoked the animal or was grossly negligent can allow exemption or reduced compensation. If management rules were broken and safety measures omitted, such as failing to use a required leash, only ‘intentional conduct by the injured party’ remains as a possible reason to reduce liability. Prohibited dangerous dogs that injure someone allow no ground for exemption. Article 89 of China's Public Security Administration Punishments Law provides a fine of up to 1000 yuan when an animal injures someone because safety precautions were not taken; more serious circumstances bring detention for 5 to 10 days. Article 30 of the Animal Epidemic Prevention Law requires regular rabies vaccination as prescribed. With the vaccination certificate issued by an animal clinic, such as a veterinary hospital, the owner must then obtain local dog registration. Outside, the dog must wear its tag and be leashed as required. Under Article 92 of the same law, failure to vaccinate as prescribed brings an order from the agriculture and rural affairs authority to correct it by a deadline, and may bring a fine of up to 1000 yuan. Continued failure brings a fine of 1000 to 5000 yuan, with an animal clinic or similar institution commissioned to handle the matter at the owner's expense.

Book note

Compensation for a dog bite includes medical expenses, lost earnings, rabies vaccine and immunoglobulin; a bill over 10000 yuan is common. Severe injuries or injuries to a child can cost more. Abandoning the dog does not end liability: the former keeper remains responsible for injuries during abandonment or escape. China's Animal Epidemic Prevention Law leaves specific dog disease-control measures to provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities. Check local dog-management rules for where to register, fees and vaccination intervals. For treatment after a bite, see Section 13, item 13 (dog and cat bites).
